messages:
alex: heads-up — i'm sketching a PRD for embeddings/rerank edge cases: dim changes, normalization, and batch semantics. want design + acceptance criteria before i file RFC. who wants in?

maria: +1. we have a customer hitting OOMs when their indexing pipeline switched dims from 512->768. they expect seamless rerank. important to capture migration story.

cheng: quick thought: do we auto-project old dims to new dims server-side or require re-indexing? auto-projection is convenient but risks quality drift.

sam: for roadmap/prio: customer asks vs platform cost. if auto-project adds CPU/GPU cost per query, need opt-in. suggest default = reject mismatch with clear error + doc'd migration path.

olivia: acceptance criteria proposal: (1) API returns 400 for mismatched dims unless client sets ?auto_project=true; (2) auto_project uses a precomputed linear map (trained offline) and adds latency <20ms p99 on dedicated; (3) tests to validate top-k rerank monotonicity within tolerance.

alex: good start. also capture batch semantics: many customers batch dozens of docs; mixed-dim examples appear. how should runtime handle batches with mixed dims?

maria: my preference: server splits mixed-dim batches by dim, processes groups, then reassembles preserving order. that avoids rejecting valid batched requests. downside: extra scheduling complexity and could increase tail latency.

cheng: agree with split-by-dim. add rule: if grouping causes >2x latency regression vs homogeneous batch, advise client to send homogeneous batches; include telemetry.

sam: product tradeoff: split-by-dim is best for UX. but add a config knob on Dedicated: max_group_splits=N or disable-splitting. For Hosted, enable by default with quota/cost notice.

olivia: normalization details: require option normalize=[true|false]; default true. spec: L2 normalize to unit norm with tolerance 1e-6. also document numeric behavior for quantized models (we should normalize in float32 after dequant).

alex: edge case: zero vectors or near-zero norm — define behavior: if norm < 1e-12, return original vector and a warning field in response. Acceptance: no crash, deterministic output.

maria: reranking acceptance criteria: end-to-end test should verify that, given identical corpus and queries, normalized vs unnormalized modes differ only by cosine vs dot semantics and we surface that in docs. include eval notebook and k=10 recall delta < 0.02 for migration tests when auto-project used.

cheng: add API contract: embeddings response includes "dim":int and "normalized":bool metadata. Server must reject/ignore mismatched dims unless auto_project flag true. Also include header X-Embed-Project-Latency with ms when projection used.

sam: rollout plan: RFC -> canary on Dedicated for one week -> gather perf + quality metrics -> opt-in Hosted beta -> full launch. Add monitoring: per-dim request rates, projection rate, per-dim p99 latency.

olivia: docs/warnings: show example code. snippet:
```
POST /v1/embeddings/batch?auto_project=true&normalize=true
{ "model": "open-embed-768", "inputs": [[...]], "meta": {...} }
```
Response includes dim and normalized flag.

alex: scope negotiation: MVP = 1) reject mismatched dims with helpful error, 2) split-by-dim batching, 3) normalization default true, 4) project-as-opt-in with offline-linear-map. advanced = automatic online retraining or LLM-based projection (future).

maria: test matrix: unit tests for split + order-preserve, integration tests with mixed dims, performance test to validate <20ms p99 projection overhead on Dedicated, fuzz tests for zero-norm, and e2e rerank quality checks.

cheng: question on storage: should we store projected embeddings in cache (KV) to avoid repeated projection? i'd say yes with TTL and metric. acceptance: cache hit reduces projection rate by 80% in our test.

sam: security/compliance: ensure projection artifacts (linear maps) are considered model artifacts and covered by model access controls. add to PRD.

olivia: i'll draft RFC with acceptance criteria and sample tests. @alex can you own rollout checklist + docs snippets?

alex: yep will do. i'll file PRD by EOD Thurs, RFC early next week. thanks all.

deploy-bot: canary job queued for eng-ml feature branch "embed-rerank-edgecase" — ETA next Tuesday.
